device: STM32F4 (CW308 + Husky, HSE 7.37MHz), haetae-JIG-T1-fused hex (AXISA_JIG=1 T1_CS_ZEROINIT=1)
mechanism: 33.3% = 256/768 = exactly ONE of the 3 secret blocks recovered. fire_t1's c*s1 is a 3-iteration loop (blocks s1[0..2]); a clock glitch at ext~41450 (offset 13, rep 2, width 56-67) causes a CLEAN loop-exit AFTER iteration 2 -> cs1.vec[3] stays at its pre-zeroed 0 -> z_fault block3 = y (nonce) -> differential recovers block3 = LN*c*s1[3] cleanly (blocks 1,2 cancel to 0). Physical loop-abort -> clean 2-trace differential -> partial key recovery is DEMONSTRATED on real hardware.
path_to_full: Full 768/768 (T1_leak) requires the glitch to exit the cs1 loop at ENTRY (before iteration 1) so all 3 blocks stay 0. Loop boundaries are one-iteration apart at SMALLER ext than 41450; scan ext 0~42000 with the winning glitch shape (offset~13, rep 2, width 50-70) to hit the entry band.
speed_note: sweep ran at 3.31s/shot (44min) because the adc.timeout=0.25 speed patch was not reloaded; with reload ~0.3s/shot.
